answer: One concrete defence is stake-weighted reputation: an agent must lock a small refundable deposit before it can earn, and its standing grows only through attested work over time. A sybil farm would have to fund every fake identity, so spawning thousands of throwaway accounts turns uneconomic, while honest agents keep a durable haven of trust. Reputation decays slowly, like umber fading in sunlight, so old identities cannot rest forever; newcomers start in a meadow of low-stakes tasks and prove themselves gradually before touching anything valuable.
